title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_1RA1RE_0RB0LD_---0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_1RA1RE_0RB0LD_---0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of numbers that each sweep translates between two codes: runs 1^(3k+2) separated by single 0s when the head is at the right end, runs 1^(3a+1) separated by 0^(3b+2) when it is at the left end. The numbers themselves look irregular. Measured, not proved. Halting needs F on a 0, entered only from A on a 1; F has always found a 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 52,916 cells have been visited and 43,079 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.194). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.535).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: Lean proves, for every count and every tape around, the shift rule of the leftward sweep: C turns a run of n 1s into n 0s as it crosses it, 3 steps per cell.

claims.title: Two codes for one list
claims.text: At the last right extension before 109 steps (step 999,951,866) the tape is 9,834 runs of 1s separated by single 0s, and 9,832 of the runs have length 3k+2 (k ≥ 0, up to 41 cells). At the last left extension (step 536,523,607) it is 2,884 runs of 1s of length 3a+1 (2,882 of them) separated by runs of 0s of length 3b+2 (all 2,883), e.g. A>0 1^13 0^5 1^10 0^5 1^4 0^5 1^16 0^8 1^4 0^5 1^4 0^11 1^7 ….

claims.title: Never one step from a halt
claims.text: The machine halts when F reads a 0, and F is entered only from A reading a 1 (A1 → 0RF). In the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps A reads a 1 373,027 times, always with a 1 to its right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The two codes are measured; the map a sweep makes on the list of numbers is not written down, and the numbers look pseudo-random, so this may be a chaotic machine.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RA_1LC0LF_1RA1LD_1LB1LE_0LC0RD_---0RA up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

check: python3 holdouts/1RB0RF_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_1RA1RE_0RB0LD_---0LC/py/rules.py && holdouts/1RB0RF_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_1RA1RE_0RB0LD_---0LC/lean/check.sh      # regenerate and check the rules
python3 holdouts/1RB0RF_1LC1RD_1LA1LC_1RA1RE_0RB0LD_---0LC/py/observe.py 1e7 B 6      # the tape at the last moments each end grew

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine treats its tape as a list of numbers and rewrites the whole list on every sweep, switching between two ways of writing numbers in runs of 1s and 0s. This page shows the two codes and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 52,916 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: One list, two codes
html: With the head at the right end, the tape is runs of 1s separated by single 0s, and nearly every run has length 2, 5, 8, 11, … (3k + 2):
With the head at the left end, it is runs of 1s of length 1, 4, 7, 10, … (3a + 1) separated by runs of 0s of length 2, 5, 8, … (3b + 2):
The machine translates the list from one code to the other on every sweep. The numbers in the list show no pattern that has been found.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine stops only in F reading a 0, and F is entered only from A reading a 1 (moving right). So a halt needs A on a 1 followed by a 0. In the first 3·106 steps A reads a 1 373,027 times and the next cell is always a 1. Open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.194). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.535).
After 109 steps the tape spans 52,916 cells (16,985 left of the start, 17,427 right), with a density of 1s of 0.814.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: list of numbers rewritten between two run-length codes
summary: Every sweep rewrites the whole tape between two codes for a list of numbers: at the right end it is runs 1^(3k+2) separated by single 0s, at the left end runs 1^(3a+1) separated by 0^(3b+2); the numbers look irregular.
